title: contributor-contracts-and-growth-ops-2026
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

This playbook defines a compact, cross-functional contributor contract that codifies day-to-day expectations, meeting norms, promotion-ready signals, benefits checkpoints, and the lean toolset new joiners should expect. It is intended for ICs, managers, and people-ops partners as a single reference for operationalizing how we work and grow at Redwood.

Why this exists

- Reduce onboarding ambiguity by giving consistent expectations across teams.
- Speed up promotion calibration with observable, role-aligned signals.
- Surface benefit and stipend touchpoints so contributors know when to act.
- Provide a minimal internal tools starter kit to remove friction during the first 30–90 days.

Scope and applicability

- Applies to all full-time and part-time contributors and their direct managers.
- Includes guidelines for remote-first collaboration, hybrid meetup norms, and asynchronous work.
- Does not replace team-specific delivery processes; it establishes a baseline contract and escalation paths.

Contributor contract (core tenets)

1) Focus on measurable outcomes

- State objectives in terms of customer or product impact (e.g., reduce inference P95 by 20% for production models, improve onboarding completion from 68% to 85%).
- Pair objectives with a short success metric and an owner.

2) Default to asynchronous first

- Use shared docs, status threads, and triaged ticket updates for work that doesn’t require immediate coordination.
- Reserve scheduled synchronous time for decisions, deep design alignment, or complex troubleshooting.

3) Transparent decision rights

- R = Responsible (author of the change), A = Approver (final sign-off), C = Consulted, I = Informed.
- Every cross-team project must publish a 1-pager that lists the RACI for critical decision points.

4) Continuous feedback loop

- Quarterly calibration conversations plus monthly 1:1s for career/development topics.
- Use short evidence-backed artifacts (PRs, dashboards, incident reviews) to illustrate impact during reviews.

Meeting and collaboration norms (practical rules)

- Default meeting length: 30 minutes. If you need more than 60 minutes, split into two focused sessions.
- Always publish a short agenda and desired outcome at least 24 hours in advance. If no agenda -> cancel.
- 10 minute rule: if the first 10 minutes are spent on status updates, switch to a written update and end.
- Camera on for 1:1s and cross-functional kickoff meetings; optional for routine working sessions.

Remote/hybrid etiquette

- Adopt inclusive practices: explicitly invite remote participants to speak, use shared notes, and avoid side conversations.
- Use local pairing rooms (virtual) for deep work pairing; book conference rooms for co-located demos only.

Career ladders: summary and promotion signals

This is a condensed guide. For full competency maps see the canonical role framework page (linked in Related Resources). Promotion readiness focuses on three pillars: delivery, craft leadership, and system-level thinking.

Levels (high-level):

- Associate / IC1: delivers scoped tasks independently, follows team processes.
- Mid / IC2: owns end-to-end features, mentors peers, contributes to system design.
- Senior / IC3: shapes project strategy across teams, drives technical choices, owns major roadmaps.
- Staff / IC4+: influences multiple teams, defines cross-product roadmaps, and represents Redwood externally for technical topics.

Promotion evidence checklist (example items managers and contributors should collect):

- Three concrete delivery artifacts (PRs, designs, release notes) with measurable outcomes.
- One cross-team collaboration example demonstrating influence beyond the immediate team.
- Mentorship outcomes: mentee progress with objective evidence (e.g., ramped a new joiner, led a hiring interview calibration).
- Impact summary: a 500–800 word narrative mapping the work to company objectives and the specific impact.

Promotion process (high level)

1. Candidate and manager prepare the evidence packet.
2. Calibration panel solicits feedback from peers and stakeholders.
3. People-ops reviews alignment with compensation banding and conducts any equity checks.
4. Final decision communicated with a development plan (if promoted, new expectations; if not, clear growth areas and timeline).

Benefits and perks: checkpoint guide

- Health and dental enrollment: complete within first 45 days. People-ops sends reminders at day 7, day 30, and day 39.
- Home office stipend: eligible upon 30-day confirmation; submit receipts via expense portal within 90 days.
- Parental leave: submit intent form to people-ops at least 8 weeks before leave start when feasible.
- Learning & conference stipend: $1,500/yr (prorated for partial-year joins). Approval required from manager; receipts due within 60 days of event.

Benefits checklist table (illustrative)

| Item | When to act | Owner for next step | Notes |
|------|-------------|---------------------|-------|
| Health enrollment | Days 0–45 | New joiner / People-ops | Auto-reminder cadence from HRIS |
| Office stipend | After day 30 | Manager & Finance | Submit receipts; shipping exceptions handled case-by-case |
| Learning stipend | Anytime | Manager approval | Encourage alignment with role growth plan |
| Commuter/parking | If eligible | New joiner | Locale-dependent programs |

Hiring and onboarding overview (how people-ops + hiring managers collaborate)

Pre-offer

- Role scoping: hiring manager drafts a 1-pager describing impact, success metrics for 6–9 months, and a calibrated level.
- Interview rubric creation: interviews must map to 3 core dimensions (execution, collaboration, technical judgment) with clear red/yellow/green outcomes.

Interview runbook (bias-mitigated steps)

1. Panel composition: at least one cross-team interviewer and one peer-level interviewer.
2. Share rubric with candidate before on-site loop when possible.
3. Score independently; panel discussion focuses on evidence.

Offer & ramp planning

- People-ops issues offer packet with a proposed 30/60/90 ramp plan template.
- Manager and new joiner agree on first project in the first 7 days and schedule onboarding pairings.

Onboarding checklist (first 30/90 days)

Day 0–7: Access and introductions

- Badge and SSO access confirmed.
- Core accounts provisioned: email, Slack, HRIS, Git, infra-console, and cost/dashboard viewers.
- Team welcome and stakeholder intro calendar scheduled.

Day 8–30: Deep context and first deliverable

- Complete mandatory security and compliance coursework.
- Pair on a small, scoped task to validate environment and pipeline access.
- One 30-day sync with people-ops to confirm benefits and role expectations.

Day 31–90: Ownership and growth plan

- Deliver first independent feature or operational improvement.
- Publish a public 90-day retrospective and next-quarter objectives.
- Career calibration conversation with manager and mentor assigned.

Internal tools starter kit (minimal list every new joiner should master)

- Slack: team channels, incident channels, on-call rosters.
- HRIS: benefits, pay stubs, time-off requests.
- Dev repo (Git): branching conventions, CI runbook URL.
- Infra dashboard: cost by token/route, latency SLO dashboards.
- Ticketing (Jira): templates for incidents, epics, and feature requests.

Access matrix (example)

| Tool | Default access | Request path | Typical SLA |
|------|----------------|--------------|-------------|
| Slack | Org-wide | None | N/A |
| HRIS | Personal | People-ops | 1–3 business days |
| Git repos | Team repo | Repo owner | 1 business day |
| Infra dashboard | Read-only by default | Infra eng request | 2 business days |
| CI/CD tokens | No | Manager + Infra sign-off | 3 business days |

Escalation and ownership

- If access issues block > 2 business days, alert people-ops and your manager; they will raise an access incident with infra.
- For delayed promotions or compensation queries, people-ops owns the escalation and will provide a 10 business day SLA for an interim response.

Manager playbook (quick prompts)

- Week 1: set clear first-project expectations and schedule 1:1 cadence.
- Week 4: check benefits enrollment and confirm office stipend workflow.
- Month 2–3: run promotion-readiness micro-review and confirm development plan.

Related resources

- Role framework and competency maps (link in Related Pages).
- How we work and decision rights (link in Related Pages).
- People-ops service catalog (search "people-ops services" in portal).

Revision history

- 2026-01-15: Initial draft authored by Maya Chen.
- 2026-03-10: Added promotion evidence checklist and benefits table (review by Priya Nair).
- 2026-06-02: Finalized onboarding checklists and access matrix (review by Ethan Alvarez).

Appendix: sample 30/60/90 template (text)

30 days: Learn - Complete docs, set up local environment, deliver a scoped bug/patch.
60 days: Contribute - Deliver a feature with end-to-end ownership and a monitoring dashboard.
90 days: Own - Drive a cross-team improvement and present a 90-day retrospective with measurable outcomes.

If you have questions about any part of this playbook, file a People-ops request or DM the author on Slack.
